answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce token stake before it earns fees, then slash that stake when a bonded claim is proven fraudulent. This makes a sybil swarm costly: creating identities is cheap, but giving each one influence requires tying up capital, and detected fraud destroys it. A nebula of accounts cannot multiply voting weight for free; like willow roots in tundra, every branch must draw on a finite resource.
